claim: Traffic signals adapt by coordinating with neighboring intersections to create 'platoons' of vehicles that can travel through multiple intersections without stopping
mechanism: Each intersection communicates its current timing and queue status to immediate neighbors. The system then adjusts signal offsets (the timing difference between adjacent signals) to create waves of green lights along major corridors. When a platoon of vehicles is detected moving through one intersection, subsequent intersections adjust their timing to allow the platoon to continue with minimal stopping
evidence: Myxomycetes create coordinated pressure waves through their networks
Traffic signal coordination has been shown to improve flow on major arterials
assumptions: Vehicle platoons can be reliably detected at intersections
Neighbors can communicate timing information effectively
Traffic patterns have some degree of predictability over short distances
expected_failure_modes: Coordination failures when neighbors have inconsistent traffic patterns
Increased delays for vehicles not part of organized platoons
Difficulty adapting to irregular traffic patterns
novelty_rationale: This hypothesis focuses on the temporal coordination aspect of the slime mold's pressure differentials, applying it to traffic signal offsets rather than just green time allocation
testability: Can be tested by measuring the percentage of vehicles that can travel through multiple consecutive signals without stopping, compared to fixed-timing systems
falsifier: If implementing this coordination system results in worse overall traffic flow because the focus on platoons creates congestion at intersection boundaries
